newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mboweni criticises S.African Reserve Bank on jobs.
newsitem.headline: Mboweni criticises S.African Reserve Bank on jobs.

text.p: Labour Minister Tito Mboweni criticised South Africa's central Reserve Bank on Friday for expressing doubts about his proposed jobs legislation in its latest quarterly bulletin.

The bulletin issued last week referred to the economy's inability to create sufficient new jobs and said the proposed Basic Conditions of Employment Bill could aggravate matters by enforcing improved terms for workers.
Mboweni, in an article in the financial daily Business Day, said the bank was entitled to comment on labour market policies but added:
"Such comments should be made judiciously, especially in cases where there is much in dispute with respect to the facts...
"The bank comment was ill-advised is easily demonstrated by the emotive reactions to it... and this in an area in which it does not have a mandate or competency."
Mboweni said bank economists had made no rigorous analysis which would allow them to assess the relationship between labour costs and employment growth.
"It is clear South Africa should not be looking to the lower ends of competitive advantage based on cheap labour but should be looking at competitive advantage which exploits other value chains.
"The current work practices and working conditions which result in a net social cost to our society may be far in excess of the presumed benefits," Mboweni said.
The Reserve Bank comments have already been criticised by the alliance of the ruling African National Congress, the Communist Party and the Congress of South African Trade Unions (Cosatu).
Cosatu has announced plans for a series of strikes to pressure business leaders during negotiations on the conditions of employment bill.
Employers say the legislation's proposals on working hours will raise labour costs and ultimately harm the interests of labour by slowing economic growth.
